Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Aerospace Dynamics Q2 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up can be found by pressing the star key followed by one on your telephone keypad. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Aerospace Dynamics' Q2 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Mark Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Lisa Moreno, Chief Strategy Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Marketing Officer; and David Kline, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning. Global Aerospace Dynamics delivered a solid performance in Q2, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across defense, commercial aerospace, space, and advanced technologies. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders.

Today, I'll highlight key areas including our overall company performance and takeaways, major new contract awards and program wins, alongside our progress in free cash flow generation, capital deployment, commercial aircraft deliveries, program margins, book-to-bill ratios, and segment guidance. These results underscore our ability to navigate supply chain challenges, capitalize on geopolitical tailwinds, and position for sustained growth.

We're particularly excited about the recent advancements in our Next Generation Air Dominance program and its potential to establish leadership in sixth-generation air dominance capabilities. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, including F-35 sustainment and hypersonic weapons, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily with rising delivery rates.

Let me start with our major new contract awards, which were exceptional this quarter. We secured over $8.7 billion in major contracts, pushing our funded backlog to a record $142 billion, up 18% year-over-year and providing more than 4.5 years of revenue visibility. On the fixed-wing side, a $3.2 billion full-rate production contract for F-35 Lot 16 center fuselages and wing boxes under Block 4 configuration builds on our prior commitments and aligns with the ramp to 156 jets annually. In hypersonics, we captured a $2.1 billion IDIQ increase for the Army's Long-Range Hypersonic Weapon with an $850 million initial task order using our Mayhem-series scramjet tech, plus a $1.4 billion sole-source for PAC-3 MSE interceptors for Qatar. Rotary-wing wins included a $1.2 billion EMD contract for Future Vertical Lift Collaborative Combat Aircraft with Kratos, tapping a $25 billion market, and a $650 million FMS deal with Poland for AH-64E upgrades. Space added a $250 million USSF EO/IR task order for resilient SATCOM. These reflect geopolitical urgency, technical leadership via $1.2 billion R&D in digital twins and directed energy, and diversification with 55% U.S. DoD, 25% FMS, and 20% commercial.

I'll now turn it over to Mark to provide more details on our financials and these performance drivers.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you, Elena, and good morning. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q2, we reported revenue of $21.2 billion, representing an 8% increase year-over-year, driven by defense ramps and commercial recovery. Our adjusted earnings per share were $2.85, exceeding expectations. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $12 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year has been raised modestly to reflect backlog strength. We are actively managing costs, investing in growth, and returning capital through dividends and repurchases.

Specific highlights include gross margin expansion to 25%, operating income of $3 billion, and free cash flow of $1.4 billion. Year-to-date FCF is $2.8 billion, on track to surpass our $5.5 billion midpoint, even against tough comps from F-35 Lot 15.

Let me expand on our overall company performance highlights and key takeaways. Despite titanium disruptions and labor shortages, revenues hit $21.2 billion, up 8%, with defense systems at 52% surging 22% on F-35 wingboxes and NGAD. Commercial aerospace grew 8% on LEAP nacelles and 787 structures, while space rose 18% with OptSat-7 and NSSL awards. Adjusted operating margins hit 12.8%, up 210 bps, EPS $2.85 up 28%, FCF 16% of revenue with DSO at 42 days. Regionally, 68% North America, 18% Europe on NATO pledges, 10% APAC on Indo-Pacific demand. R&D at 6.3% unveiled 150kW directed energy and eVTOL batteries. Backlog 2.8 years visibility, ROIC 18.2%. Key takeaways: balanced portfolio superiority, $500 million repurchases, Q4 revenue $2.95-3.05 billion.

Diving into free cash flow generation and utilization, this remains a hallmark. Q2 FCF $1.4 billion, up 56% from $900 million, from $2.1 billion operating cash up 42%, offset by $700 million CapEx below plan. TTM yield 8.2% above peers. Drivers: defense revenue $4.2 billion up 18% on NGAD and hypersonics, F-35 sustainment $450 million high-margin. Working capital: DSO 52 days via ERP, inventory turns 4.2x liquidating $300 million spares. Commercial: 737 MAX/A320neo at 25/month converting 28% of $18 billion backlog as travel hits 102% 2019. CapEx: 40% NGAD facility, 30% digital twins cutting prototyping 22%, 20% additive titanium. Diversified: 75% U.S. FY24 NDAA, 12% Europe Eurofighter/F-35, APAC GCAP/MQ-9B. Utilization: $1.1 billion returns YTD, dividend $0.45/share up 12.5% yielding 1.8%, $800 million buybacks retiring 2.1% shares. Prepaid $900 million debt, net debt/EBITDA 1.8x. $500 million organic hypersonics/AI, $400 million M&A like smallsat propulsion. FY24 FCF $5.3-5.7 billion reaffirmed.

On program margins and cost performance, consolidated margins expanded 130 bps to 10.8%. Defense fixed-wing 12.4% on $2.8 billion, F-47 CPI 1.05, $120 million underruns from composites, offset $45 million legacy loss. Missiles 11.1% CPI 1.08, $200 million favorable from GaN, $30 million rare earth provision. Commercial 7.2% on $3.1 billion, break-even GAD-900 CPI 0.98, $80 million avionics adjustment. Space 9.5%, rotary 10.2%. Cost growth 3.2% below peers, labor productivity +8%, fixed-price 55%. Guide Q3 11.0-11.5%, FY 10.5-11.0% to 12%+ 2025.

Book-to-bill was 1.18x overall, $4.2 billion orders vs $3.55 billion revenue, backlog $28.7 billion up 14%. Commercial 1.06x on $1.48 billion bookings including Delta 737s. Defense 1.32x on F-35 radars, UK Tempest. Missiles 1.45x on JASSM/LRASM, Saudi. Space 1.22x on NASA/ESA. Three-quarter trailing 1.15x.

Commercial aircraft deliveries: 142 units Q2, +28% YoY, 112 single-aisle, 30 widebody. YTD 268 toward 550-600 FY, 92% 2019 recovery. Backlog $492 billion, 4,800 slots. NA 45% +35%, Europe 25% GTF issues, APAC 20% +50%, ME/LATAM 10%. Mitigations: digital twins -17% defects, AFP 20% cost-out, SAF kits. Aftermarket +32%.

Capital deployment: FCF $1.2 billion H1 up 18%. Framework: 40% organic $480 million digital twins/high-energy lasers/Viper autonomy, APAC backlog $18 billion +22%. Dividends 28-year streak, $0.65/share +8% yield 2.1%, 42% payout. Buybacks $850 million 4.2 million shares, +$2.5 billion authorized, TSR 28% YTD. M&A $1.1 billion: SpectraForge GaN radars +200 bps, avionics carve-out $120 million revenue. Dry powder $1-2 billion PNT/AI for Poland/GCC.

Finally, revenue and earnings guidance by segment. Defense $36.5-37.5 billion revenue, $5.6-5.9 billion profit 15.2-15.7% on F-35/HAWC/PAC-3. Space $23.8-24.5 billion, $3.4-3.6 billion 14.3-14.7% on GPS/NRO/Vulcan. Aviation $25-26 billion, $2.9-3.1 billion 11.6-11.9% aftermarket mix. Total FY $85.3-88 billion, 14.0-14.3% margins, FCF $6.5-7 billion.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Mark. Operationally, we've seen significant supply chain improvements, ramping deliveries on F-35 and hypersonics with 95% on-time rates. Investments in automation and digital tools like Siemens NX have boosted efficiency, reducing prototyping costs 22% and inventory turns to 4.2x. Our Fort Worth and Renton facilities are at 95% capacity with 3,500 new hires via apprenticeships.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. On technology, we're advancing next-generation propulsion with adaptive cycle engines and scramjets achieving Mach 5+, plus AI-optimized guidance for hypersonics and loyal wingman autonomy. Digital twins and additive manufacturing give us a competitive edge, de-risking NGAD and directed energy lasers at 300kW.

Lisa Moreno:
Thank you, Raj. Strategically, we're evaluating tuck-in acquisitions like recent smallsat propulsion to expand space and counter-drone tech, targeting 10-12% IRR amid $1.2 trillion global defense spend. New models leverage AUKUS and GCAP for Indo-Pacific growth.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Lisa. Marketing-wise, our campaigns are driving brand resonance, with digital channels boosting awareness among DoD and airlines. Results show 25% higher engagement on NGAD and commercial MRO messaging.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Instructions for questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from Jamie Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jamie Carter:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the major new contract awards, particularly NGAD positioning?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Certainly, Jamie. These $8.7 billion wins strategically position us for NGAD with F-35 digital flyover accelerating design 30%. Hypersonics $2.1 billion leverages Mayhem scramjets with 20% CEP reduction via AI, tied to AUKUS and Taiwan needs. Poland's Apache $650 million taps NATO rearmament, adding 8% international backlog share. $180 billion pipeline at 40% win probability eyes 12-15% FY25 growth. Multi-year authorities now 65%, 85% domestic sourcing.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim:
Hi, thanks. Curious about free cash flow utilization and capital returns plans?

Mark Thompson:
Rachel, our FCF strength enables balanced allocation. YTD $1.1 billion shareholder returns: dividends up 12.5%, buybacks at $285 average retiring 2.1% shares, ROIC >15%. Debt deleveraged to 1.8x, freeing organic investments like $500 million hypersonics wind tunnels and AI. $400 million M&A for space verticalization. FY repurchases $1.5-2 billion scaled to yield, with TSR outpacing peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Lopez:
Regarding the commercial aircraft delivery rates and recovery?

Mark Thompson:
Mike, deliveries at 142 Q2, pacing 550-600 FY with 92% recovery. Single-aisles 98%, widebodies 82%. Demand-supply mismatch with RPKs 102%, backlog $492 billion 22 months. APAC +50% on IndiGo/ICBC. Digital Factory of the Future -15 aircraft/month uplift by Q2 2025, LEAN compressing FAT to 16 days. Dual-use to UAS, $1.2 billion R&D for NMA/ZEROe spillovers. Risks hedged with $15 billion backlog.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Singh with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Laura Singh:
Question about book-to-bill and segment guidance updates?

Lisa Moreno:
Laura, 1.18x overall drives backlog growth, defense 1.32x on DoD FY24 $850 billion, missiles 1.45x Ukraine/Rea Sea. Guidance raised: defense $36.5-37.5 billion 15.2% margins on Patriot/NGAD; space $23.8-24.5 billion on pLEO; aviation steady aftermarket tilt. Total $85.3-88 billion, FCF $6.5-7 billion. FY25 tailwinds $923 billion NDAA +10% hypersonics.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
